title: Choose the visual world for Graph Explorer
question: Every card is a complete visual system grounded in what an intro-stats student already knows. Pick one, steer, or re-roll. Charts inside the canvases keep the backend's colors in every direction.

options.label: Stat Plot
options.lineage: the TI-84 STAT PLOT and LinReg screens every student has stared at
options.thesis: The explorer is a graphing calculator screen grown to laptop size: a readout line of truth, soft keys along the bottom, and nothing decorative.
options.viewport: A dark bezel frames one LCD-toned panel. Top: a one-line readout, 'LinReg  y = 0.89x − 0.01   r = 0.98'. Middle: scatter plate left, line plate right, same height and baseline. Below: the plain-language sentences as readout rows. Bottom: five soft keys — X AXIS, Y AXIS, SIZE, TRACE, EXPORT.
options.risk: Reads as retro novelty if the type is pixel-faked or the keys get cute; the bezel must stay thin and the sentences must stay real prose.

raised.raise: State lives in line form, not hue: data solid, fit dashed, stale half-tone. No second accent is ever needed.
Scatter and line plates share one exact height and baseline, so the eye compares without re-reading axes.
One alert tone is reserved for change: when axes switch, each sentence that changed holds a highlight until the next change.
Vast unprinted ground: the scatter owns the field and chrome is a thin rail.
Labels are one fixed size everywhere; the selected series burns brightest in the line plate.
The active axis choice is marked like a pen circle, visible from across the room in the demo video.

regions.label: X AXIS | Y AXIS | SIZE | TRACE | EXPORT

options.label: Notebook Cell
options.lineage: the Jupyter notebook the student already works in
options.thesis: The explorer is one notebook: an In cell where you choose columns, an Out cell where the charts and the sentences appear.
options.viewport: A left gutter runs the full height. In[1]: two selects and a size field, set like code. Out[1]: scatter left, line right, same baseline. Out[2]: the sentences as a monospaced result block with the stats table beside it. A 'Download' control sits in the Out gutter like a cell action.
options.risk: This is the direction most runs for a student audience land on; it will feel instantly familiar and may read as 'just a notebook' to course staff.

options.label: Emission Line Rail
options.lineage: a glass spectrogram on a viewing box
options.thesis: Everything hangs off one off-centre rail; colour exists only as seven hairlines.
options.viewport: A banded charcoal field with the chart as a plate hanging off a calibrated rail.
options.case: Students do not identify with spectrograms, and state-by-line-form on a dark field hides the task.
options.kept: State carried in line form (solid, dashed, half-height), never in hue.
options.risk: Beautiful and illegible for a first-time viewer.

options.label: Hall Catalog
options.lineage: a convention circle catalog on newsprint
options.thesis: Thousands of stamp-sized cells, the chosen ones circled in pen.
options.viewport: A packed grid of column thumbnails with the active pair circled.
options.case: Four columns do not make a catalog; the grid has nothing to fill.
options.kept: The active choice is marked like a pen circle, unmistakable at a glance.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.lineage: one plant through five seasons on fixed-scale plates
options.thesis: Plates at exactly the same scale and ground so change is directly comparable.
options.viewport: Cream plates on one shared baseline with engraved captions.
options.case: The registration discipline is exactly right for two charts; the cream-and-engraving world is wrong for a stats student at a laptop.
options.kept: Both chart plates share one exact height and baseline.
options.risk: Reads as a herbarium, not a tool.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: a boarding pass beside a live departures board
options.thesis: One alert colour reserved for change; a changed row moves and stays lit until noticed.
options.viewport: A ranked board of rows, one just re-ranked and glowing.
options.case: There is no ranking to watch here; the carrier is empty. The change-hold behaviour is worth keeping.
options.kept: One alert tone for change, held until the next change.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.lineage: a matte black record sleeve with a white pulsar plot and a fac number
options.thesis: Vast black, one plot owning the field, names replaced by colour codes.
options.viewport: A black field with a single white line stack and a tiny catalogue number.
options.case: Replacing labels with codes contradicts a product whose whole point is sentences; the restraint is worth keeping.
options.kept: Vast unprinted ground: the chart owns the field.
options.risk: Hides exactly what the student came for.

options.label: Transit Diagram
options.thesis: Coloured lines at disciplined angles, the chosen line burning brightest.
options.viewport: A dark blue field with routes as the whole composition.
options.case: The backend's charts are not route diagrams, and a dark enamel ground fights white chart canvases.
options.kept: Fixed-size labels; the selected series burns brightest.
options.risk: Dark ground versus white canvases is a visible seam.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean analytics dashboard: sidebar of selects, two chart cards, a stats card, one blue accent.
canonCard.viewport: Left sidebar with dataset, x and y selects. Two chart cards side by side. A stats and description card below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other chart tool by design.
